description: Surviving mutants a maintainer has looked at and accepted: equivalent ones (no input can tell them apart from the original) and ones that only make a check stricter. mutation_check.py leaves these out of its report. An entry matches by module, cosmic-ray operator and the stripped text of the source line, so it follows the line when code above it moves and stops matching when the line itself changes. tests/test_mutation_check.py fails when an entry's line no longer exists. Say in reason why the mutant cannot matter.

accepted.reason: How long cosmic-ray waits for one mutant's tests is a tuning value; 119 or 121 seconds changes no outcome a test can observe.

In spells_a_gated_name() the flattened reading differs from the text only where an unquoted extglob group became *, so a string raw_words() rejects as typed (its stand-in character anywhere, or a quoted character the lexer drops) is rejected flattened too, unless that character sits inside the group. Stopping at the first rejection then skips only a command-string prefilter on a string the gate cannot split; no test input reaches that case, and the outer command is still read flattened by refusal().

accepted.line: for reading in (text, *(flattened[:1] if flattened else ())):
accepted.reason: The surviving variant is [:2], which also reads the extglob group's own text as a command string. That only adds a reading to a check whose readings each can only add a refusal, so it is stricter, never weaker; the [:0] variant, which drops the flattened reading, is killed.
How long build() waits before retrying a dropped base pull is a tuning value; 14 or 16 seconds changes no outcome a test can observe, and the tests read the constant rather than restating it.
